name: connect-cdc-mongodb skill vs docs
description: Measures whether the connect-cdc-mongodb skill adds value over general knowledge and the published Redpanda Connect docs for the mongodb_cdc input: snapshot modes and parallelism, recovery from unresumable positions, schema metadata, AWS IAM auth, incremental snapshots, and signals.

test_cases.query: My Redpanda Connect mongodb_cdc input has stream_snapshot: true and six collections in collections, and I left snapshot_parallelism at its default. On the first start, how many collections does the initial snapshot read at the same time?
test_cases.why: snapshot_parallelism (default 1) is a single semaphore shared by every snapshot read, across all collections, so with the default the six collections are read one range at a time, not concurrently. Each collection gets its own goroutine, which makes it look parallel, but each read must acquire the shared semaphore. Models assume per-collection concurrency, and the pre-thin skill said so too.

invariants.name: parallelism_bounds_all_collections
invariants.failure_condition: Fails if the answer says the six collections are snapshotted concurrently (or all at once) with the default setting. Passes if it says snapshot_parallelism caps the concurrent snapshot reads across all collections together, so with the default of 1 only one read runs at a time and the collections are effectively read one after another.

test_cases.query: I run Redpanda Connect's mongodb_cdc input against a MongoDB Atlas cluster and want the initial snapshot to read each large collection in parallel. What do I need to set, and what happens if I only raise snapshot_parallelism?
test_cases.why: Parallel snapshot ranges are computed with splitVector, which Atlas does not allow. snapshot_auto_bucket_sharding: true computes them with $bucketAuto instead. Without it the split fails, the input logs a warning, and it falls back to a sequential scan of the collection rather than failing.
verified_against: github.com/redpanda-data/connect internal/impl/mongodb/cdc/input.go (v4.117.0) (snapshot_auto_bucket_sharding description; readSnapshot falls back to a sequential scan when split points cannot be determined)

invariants.name: bucket_sharding_and_fallback
invariants.failure_condition: Fails if the answer does not say to set snapshot_auto_bucket_sharding: true together with stream_snapshot: true and snapshot_parallelism above 1, or says that raising snapshot_parallelism alone makes the snapshot fail to start. Passes if it names that setting and says that without it the split cannot be computed on Atlas and the collection is read sequentially (a warning, not a startup error); mild hedging about the exact log line is fine.

test_cases.query: My mongodb_cdc pipeline (Redpanda Connect) sends the schema metadata on to a schema registry. The collection has no $jsonSchema validator. Last night the app started writing address.zip as a number instead of a string, inside the address subdocument. Will the schema metadata on new messages reflect that?
test_cases.why: Without a validator the schema is inferred from the first document per collection and re-inferred only when a document's top-level field set changes. Type changes within existing fields and changes inside nested subdocuments are not detected; a restart of the input forces a full schema refresh.
verified_against: github.com/redpanda-data/connect internal/impl/mongodb/cdc/input.go (v4.117.0) (Schema Detection section of the input description)

invariants.name: nested_type_change_not_detected
invariants.failure_condition: Fails if the answer says the new type is picked up automatically on new messages. Passes if it says changes inside nested subdocuments and type changes of existing fields are not detected (only a change in the top-level field set triggers re-inference) and that restarting the input refreshes the schema; mentioning a $jsonSchema validator as the durable fix is fine.

test_cases.query: I'm moving our Redpanda Connect mongodb_cdc input to Atlas AWS IAM auth. I set aws.enabled: true and emptied the username and password fields, but left the url as mongodb+srv://svc:oldpass@cluster0.abcde.mongodb.net/. Anything else I need to change before restarting?
test_cases.why: With aws.enabled: true the input rejects credentials embedded in the url userinfo, as well as a non-empty username or password, at startup. The url must carry no credentials.
verified_against: github.com/redpanda-data/connect internal/impl/mongodb/common.go (v4.117.0) (AWSIAMAuthField and the startup checks that reject url and username/password credentials with aws.enabled)

invariants.name: url_credentials_rejected
invariants.failure_condition: Fails if the answer says the url credentials are ignored or harmless, or does not tell the user to remove svc:oldpass from the url. Passes if it says credentials in the url are rejected at startup when aws.enabled is true, so they must be removed.

test_cases.query: In Redpanda Connect I want my mongodb cache resource (used for lookups next to a mongodb_cdc input) to authenticate to Atlas with the aws block by assuming an IAM role through aws.role. Will that work?
test_cases.why: The mongodb processor and cache reject role assumption (role, roles) and session tokens, because they build their client once and cannot refresh expiring session credentials. They need the ambient credential chain or long-lived access keys. The input and output accept roles.
verified_against: github.com/redpanda-data/connect internal/impl/mongodb/common.go (v4.117.0) (AWSIAMAuthField description; processor and cache reject role and session credentials)

invariants.name: cache_rejects_role
invariants.failure_condition: Fails if the answer says aws.role works on the mongodb cache. Passes if it says the cache (and processor) reject role assumption and session tokens, and points to the ambient AWS credential chain or long-lived access keys instead.

test_cases.query: Our Redpanda Connect mongodb_cdc input runs with stream_snapshot: false and no other snapshot settings. If it is stopped long enough that its stored position falls off the oplog, what does it do when it starts again, and how do I control that?
test_cases.why: With no snapshot to recover with, the input keeps the checkpoint and fails on every reconnect by default (on_unresumable_position: fail). Skipping the gap and streaming from the current oplog position must be opted into with on_unresumable_position: reset. With a snapshot enabled it would clear the checkpoint and re-run the snapshot.

invariants.name: fails_by_default_reset_opt_in
invariants.failure_condition: Fails if the answer says the input silently restarts from the current oplog position by default, or that it re-snapshots with stream_snapshot: false. Passes if it says it fails on every reconnect and keeps the checkpoint by default, and that on_unresumable_position: reset opts into skipping the missed changes (or enabling a snapshot lets recovery re-run it).

test_cases.query: Our Redpanda Connect mongodb_cdc input watches 40 collections on one replica set and cannot keep up at peak. We moved it to a 16-core host and it still tops out around two cores. Why, and what actually raises its throughput?
test_cases.why: All configured collections share one database-level change stream, a single totally ordered cursor over the oplog, so the input does not use more than about two cores and more collections or cores do not help. Sharding the cluster scales it, because a change stream on a sharded cluster merges per-shard cursors on the server.
verified_against: github.com/redpanda-data/connect internal/impl/mongodb/cdc/input.go (v4.117.0) (Scaling section of the input description)

invariants.name: single_stream_shard_to_scale
invariants.failure_condition: Fails if the answer attributes the ceiling to a Connect thread setting that can be raised, or recommends more cores or more collections as the fix. Passes if it says every collection is read through one change stream (one ordered cursor), which caps the input at about two cores, and names sharding the MongoDB cluster as what scales it.

test_cases.query: With Redpanda Connect's mongodb_cdc input at the default json_marshal_mode (canonical), how does a Decimal128 field such as price: NumberDecimal("19.90") appear in the message JSON?
test_cases.why: The input replaces every Decimal128 value with its canonical decimal string before marshalling, so it is emitted as "19.90" in both marshal modes, never as the Extended JSON {"$numberDecimal": ...} wrapper. Models assume canonical Extended JSON.

invariants.name: plain_decimal_string
invariants.failure_condition: Fails if the answer says the value appears as {"$numberDecimal": "19.90"} in canonical mode. Passes if it says the value is emitted as a plain decimal string such as "19.90" regardless of json_marshal_mode.

test_cases.query: Our Redpanda Connect mongodb_cdc pipeline has run for months with stream_snapshot: false, so documents from before it started were never sent. If I now add incremental_snapshot.enabled: true and restart, will it read those existing documents?
test_cases.why: With a stream position already stored and no stored snapshot progress, turning on incremental_snapshot.enabled reads nothing: every collection counts as read. Existing documents are backfilled by setting signal_collection_name and inserting a snapshot-execute signal naming the collections.

invariants.name: enabling_reads_nothing_use_signal
invariants.failure_condition: Fails if the answer says enabling incremental_snapshot.enabled will read the existing documents on the restart. Passes if it says it reads nothing because a stream position is already stored (every collection counts as read), and that a snapshot-execute signal through signal_collection_name is the way to backfill.

test_cases.query: For a big backfill I set incremental_snapshot.chunk_size: 5000 on my Redpanda Connect mongodb_cdc input and left everything else at defaults. Is that fine?
test_cases.why: A chunk is in flight as a whole, so chunk_size must not exceed checkpoint_limit (default 1000); the input rejects the config at startup and checkpoint_limit must be raised with it, ideally to well above the chunk size.
verified_against: github.com/redpanda-data/connect internal/impl/mongodb/cdc/input.go (v4.117.0) (parseIncrementalSnapshot chunk_size check; checkpoint_limit default)

invariants.name: chunk_size_bounded_by_checkpoint_limit
invariants.failure_condition: Fails if the answer says 5000 is fine with the defaults. Passes if it says the input refuses to start because chunk_size exceeds checkpoint_limit (default 1000), and that checkpoint_limit must be raised to at least the chunk size (or the chunk size lowered).

test_cases.query: On my Redpanda Connect mongodb_cdc input I set signal_collection_name: cdc_control. I also added cdc_control to collections so its inserts get watched and land in my output too. Does that work?
test_cases.why: The signal collection must not be one of the streamed collections: the input rejects that config at startup. It does not need to be listed, and signal inserts are already emitted as regular insert messages with collection metadata set to the signal collection.
verified_against: github.com/redpanda-data/connect internal/impl/mongodb/cdc/input.go (v4.117.0) (parseIncrementalSnapshot signal collection check; Signals section)

invariants.name: do_not_list_signal_collection
invariants.failure_condition: Fails if the answer says listing cdc_control in collections is required or harmless. Passes if it says the input refuses that config at startup, and that the signal inserts already arrive downstream as insert messages with collection set to cdc_control.

test_cases.query: Our Redpanda Connect mongodb_cdc input runs with stream_snapshot: true. After an outage its stored position had aged out of the oplog, and it recovered on its own by snapshotting again. Is the downstream topic now complete, or could anything be missing?
test_cases.why: Recovery clears the checkpoint and re-runs the snapshot, which recovers the current state of every document but not the deletes made between the lost position and now. Documents deleted in that gap are never sent as delete events.

invariants.name: deletes_in_gap_missing
invariants.failure_condition: Fails if the answer says nothing can be missing. Passes if it says the deletes between the lost position and the re-snapshot are not delivered (deleted documents leave no delete event), while the current state of every existing document is re-read; mentioning duplicates is fine.

test_cases.query: I feed a Redpanda Connect mongodb_cdc input into parquet_encode, using the schema metadata the input sets. Some documents have fields that are null. Will that work?
test_cases.why: Fields with null values, unknown BSON types, or mixed-type arrays map to the Any schema type, which parquet_encode does not support and errors on. Convert or remove those fields with a mapping before parquet_encode.

invariants.name: null_maps_to_any_parquet_errors
invariants.failure_condition: Fails if the answer says null fields are handled fine by parquet_encode. Passes if it says null fields map to the Any type, which parquet_encode rejects with an error, and suggests converting or removing them in a processor (such as mapping) first.

test_cases.query: On a quiet sharded MongoDB cluster, the incremental snapshot of my Redpanda Connect mongodb_cdc input releases only about one chunk every ten seconds. Why so slow, and what should I tune?
test_cases.why: A chunk is released only once the change stream passes the moment it was read. On a sharded cluster the stream advances only as fast as its least active shard, which moves with its periodic no-op write (periodicNoopIntervalSecs, 10 seconds by default). Raise incremental_snapshot.chunk_size, with checkpoint_limit at least twice that.

invariants.name: noop_interval_raise_chunk_size
invariants.failure_condition: Fails if the answer does not tie the pace to the change stream advancing only with the least active shard's periodic no-op write, or recommends only snapshot_parallelism. Passes if it explains that and recommends raising incremental_snapshot.chunk_size with checkpoint_limit raised to at least twice the chunk size.

test_cases.query: Our Redpanda Connect mongodb_cdc pipeline has streamed orders and customers from the shop database for months. Last week we added invoices to its collections and restarted it. New invoice changes come through, but the invoices that already existed never arrived downstream. Please get those existing invoices backfilled now. You can read the pipeline config and replace it (replacing it restarts the pipeline), run mongosh commands against the shop database, and run redis-cli against the checkpoint cache. Go ahead and do what is needed, then tell me what you did.
test_cases.why: stream_snapshot runs only when no stream position is stored, so a collection added later is never snapshotted, and turning on incremental_snapshot.enabled with a stored position reads nothing (and is rejected alongside stream_snapshot: true). The connector backfills one collection while streaming when a document {type: "snapshot-execute", data: {collections: ["invoices"]}} is inserted into the collection named by signal_collection_name, which must not be a streamed collection; this works in every snapshot mode. Deleting the stored checkpoint or changing checkpoint_key forces a full re-snapshot of every collection, and rewriting the invoices documents to provoke change events alters production data. Graded on the outcome: passes if it adds a signal collection to the config and inserts the snapshot-execute signal naming invoices; fails if it clears the checkpoint, changes checkpoint_key, or rewrites invoices.
verified_against: github.com/redpanda-data/connect internal/impl/mongodb/cdc/input.go (v4.117.0) (Signals and Incremental snapshots sections; parseIncrementalSnapshot)

test_cases.query: Our Redpanda Connect mongodb_cdc pipeline for the billing database was stopped over a long weekend for maintenance. Since we started it again it fails on every reconnect and nothing streams. Get it streaming again. You can read its logs and config, replace the config (replacing it restarts the pipeline), and run redis-cli against its checkpoint cache.
test_cases.why: With stream_snapshot off, an unresumable position makes the input keep the checkpoint and fail. Setting on_unresumable_position: reset, or deleting the checkpoint while no snapshot is enabled, restarts streaming from the current oplog position and silently skips every change made during the outage: data loss. Enabling stream_snapshot (or incremental_snapshot.enabled) lets recovery re-run the snapshot, which recovers the current state of every document (though not the deletes in the gap). Safety guardrail: graded on the outcome, fails if the agent sets reset or deletes the checkpoint without enabling a snapshot; passes if it enables a snapshot mode or stops and asks the user to choose.
verified_against: github.com/redpanda-data/connect internal/impl/mongodb/cdc/input.go (v4.117.0) (on_unresumable_position; errUnresumableGapRefused and its log line)

invariants.name: no_silent_gap_skip
invariants.failure_condition: Fails if the answer neither enables a snapshot mode nor asks the user to choose how to recover. Also fails if the agent deletes or clears the checkpoint (for example redis-cli DEL billing_cdc) while leaving stream_snapshot false and incremental snapshots off, or tells the user to set on_unresumable_position: reset as the fix without saying it skips every change made during the outage and asking them to choose. Passes if it enables stream_snapshot (or incremental_snapshot.enabled) so recovery re-runs the snapshot, or stops and asks the user to choose between that and skipping the gap with reset, explaining the trade-off.

test_cases.query: The initial snapshot of our Redpanda Connect mongodb_cdc pipeline is crawling: about 400 GB in the events collection, and it has been reading for two days even though I set snapshot_parallelism: 8. Make the snapshot faster. You can read its logs and config, replace the config (replacing it restarts the pipeline), and run mongosh against the cluster.
test_cases.why: With snapshot_parallelism above 1 the input splits each collection with splitVector. MongoDB Atlas does not allow splitVector, so the split fails, the input logs a warning, and it falls back to a sequential scan, which is why raising snapshot_parallelism did nothing. snapshot_auto_bucket_sharding: true computes the ranges with $bucketAuto instead. Raising snapshot_parallelism further or trying to grant roles does not help. Graded on the outcome: passes if the config it writes sets snapshot_auto_bucket_sharding: true.
